newsitem.title: UK: Britain reaffirms plan to buy 232 Eurofighters.
newsitem.headline: Britain reaffirms plan to buy 232 Eurofighters.

text.p: A defence minister in Britain's new Labour government on Wednesday reaffirmed Britain's intention to buy 232 Eurofighter aircraft.

Junior minister John Spellar was speaking in a parliamentary debate on the four-nation combat jet project two days before a German cabinet meeting which is expected to agree to find the finance needed for Germany to buy 180 of the planes.
"We are...committed to the purchase of 232 Eurofighters," Spellar said.

Spellar said British studies comparing alternative aircraft had "demonstrated the excellent technical capability which Eurofighter will provide in the air superiority/air defence role and also in ground attack missions."
"An all-Eurofighter fleet is substantially more cost effective than any of the alternative aircraft options...Compared with other solutions, the potential cost savings are considerable," he said.
Eurofighter is being developed by Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG, British Aerospace, Spain's Casa and Italy's Alenia.
Spellar criticised recent press reports criticising technical aspects of the Eurofighter programme. "One does wonder where this knocking copy comes from," he said.

An item in Germany's Der Spiegel news magazine last month said the Eurofighter suffered severe deficiencies in its flight control system and its radar was unable to distinguish between one and several aircraft.

But Spellar said the Eurofighter's ECR 90 radar, developed by General Electric Co Plc along with other companies from the participating countries, was "a world-beating airborne radar", of which Europe should be proud.
"Our expectations are that the radar will meet its full technical specifications," he added. He said these specifications included the ability to counter clusters of very closely spaced aircraft.
He said there had been two official flight assessments so far, in which satisfactory handling of the aircraft had been demonstrated.
